panel-black.note: Declared as --bg2 in :root but not applied to any surface in the three shipped pages (home, about, work/*) as of this scan — dormant, not an active layering rule.

display.purpose: Home page h1 only — the single most important surface, 74px ceiling.

display-secondary.purpose: h1 shared identically by the two case-study pages (pragma, FinanceTracker), 60px ceiling.

display-tertiary.purpose: About page h1, the site's long-form reading surface, 52px ceiling.

title.purpose: Card and component titles: case-study h3, decision h3, pipeline-stage name, app name, app category headline.

body.purpose: Primary paragraph copy: page subheads, 'what it proves' sections, and About-page long-form prose.

small.purpose: Secondary card copy, inline links, stat lines, read-more affordances, technical-skill row text, footer copyright line.

micro.purpose: Pipeline-stage numbers on the pragma page. Verified 400 weight (inherited, no explicit font-weight set). The 'Human approval' badge is a separate, deliberately more emphatic 600/uppercase treatment, not this token.

label.purpose: Header nav links only. No eyebrow/kicker role exists in this system (banned sitewide during finish review). The footer no longer carries a link list; it is copyright-only, set at Small.

shadows.name: icon-lift
shadows.purpose: Grounds a small raster app icon image against a flat card in the homepage Shipped Apps grid.

shadows.name: cta-hover
shadows.purpose: Resume button hover state — the one 'about to be pressed' shadow in the system.

shadows.name: glass-highlight
shadows.purpose: Soft top edge catch-light on every glass card, so the translucency reads even where the ground behind it is close to flat.

motion.name: ease-supporting
motion.purpose: Calm exponential ease-out for the general .fade-in entrance (paragraphs, cards, nav, images). Pure decelerate, no overshoot — differentiation from the signature curve is speed/distance/scale, not literal spring physics.

motion.name: ease-signature
motion.purpose: Faster, steeper exponential ease-out reserved for .spring-in, applied only to each page's h1 — paired with a larger 30px rise and a .95→1 scale for a genuinely distinct, punchier arrival than supporting content, without bounce.

components.name: Focus State
components.description: Keyboard-focus outline for every link and button. Mouse clicks never trigger it (:focus-visible only).

components.name: Primary Button (Resume CTA)
components.description: The only filled, non-glass component in the system — used once, for the resume download.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-block; background: #C9A15A; color: #0A0A0C; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; padding: 11px 20px; border-radius: 8px; text-decoration: none; transition: transform .25s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), box-shadow .25s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); box-shadow: 0 6px 20px rgba(201,161,90,.25); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #C9A15A; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Static Card
components.description: Default glass card for decorative, non-clickable content (pipeline stages, architecture decisions). No hover state — the absence of interactivity is the point.

components.css: .ds-card { border-radius: 14px; background: rgba(255,255,255,.055); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.09); backdrop-filter: blur(14px) saturate(1.3); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.05); padding: 18px 16px; } .ds-card-label { font-size: 11px; color: #8A8A92; } .ds-card-title { font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; color: #F2F2F0; margin-top: 6px; } .ds-card-body { font-size: 13px; color: #8A8A92; margin-top: 6px; line-height: 1.4; }

components.name: Interactive Card
components.description: Glass card wrapped in a real <a> link (case studies, apps) — the only cards that ever show a hover affordance. No kicker/tag above the h3 — the heading carries its own weight (No-Kicker Rule).
components.html:
pragma — the agentic pipeline

An 8-agent iOS development pipeline: spec → plan → feature → gates → review → test → bugfix → release.
components.css: .ds-card-interactive { display: block; text-decoration: none; color: inherit; border-radius: 14px; background: rgba(255,255,255,.055); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.09); backdrop-filter: blur(14px) saturate(1.3); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.05); padding: 26px; transition: border-color .4s ease, transform .5s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), background .4s ease; } .ds-card-interactive:hover { border-color: rgba(201,161,90,.4); transform: translateY(-3px); background: rgba(255,255,255,.06); } .ds-card-h3 { margin: 0 0 8px; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; color: #F2F2F0; } .ds-card-p { margin: 0; font-size: 13px; color: #8A8A92; line-height: 1.6; }

components.name: Nav Link
components.description: Header navigation item — three states: rest, hover, active (aria-current). The nav is now the site's only link list (About Me, Resume, LinkedIn, Email, GitHub); the footer carries no links.
components.html: About MeResume
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; gap: 22px; } .ds-nav-link { font-size: 12px; color: #8A8A92; text-decoration: none; letter-spacing: .01em; transition: color .25s ease; padding: 14px 2px; } .ds-nav-link:hover { color: #F2F2F0; } .ds-nav-link.is-active { color: #C9A15A; }

components.name: Brand Mark
components.description: Header logo — a 32×32 image badge (/favicon.svg), replacing a former text wordmark. Lifts 1px on hover using the supporting-motion easing.
components.css: .ds-brand { display: inline-flex; padding: 4px 0; line-height: 0; } .ds-brand img { display: block; transition: transform .25s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); } .ds-brand:hover img { transform: translateY(-1px); }

components.name: Evidence Image (case thumbnail / session / screenshot gallery)
components.description: Shared shape language for all three real-image patterns on the site: home-page case thumbnails (16:9), the pragma session capture (native ratio), and the FinanceTracker screenshot gallery (368:800, 4-up grid).
components.css: .ds-shots { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4,1fr); gap: 14px; } .ds-shots img { width: 100%; height: auto; aspect-ratio: 368/800; object-fit: cover; border-radius: 14px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.09); display: block; }

components.name: Section Headline
components.description: The h2 used to label a group of cards (e.g. 'Case studies', 'Shipped apps', 'The pipeline'). Plain sentence case at the Headline step — no uppercase-kicker pattern.

narrative.overview: This system exists to make one claim credible: that the work behind it is real, current, and production-grade — not a template dressed up for a job search. Every visual decision serves legibility and verification first. The palette stays almost entirely neutral (near-black ground, off-white text, muted ash for secondary content) with exactly one warm accent, spent with discipline rather than scattered for energy. Where the system reaches for personality, it reaches toward the subject's own world — SF Pro as the display and body face throughout, because the person this site represents builds native Apple software, not because it is a safe default. The direction was chosen through three real rounds of iteration: round one (flat hero + plain grid) was rejected as static and boring; round two (fluorescent poster, drum-machine sequencer, notation score) was rejected as too provocative for a senior hiring audience. What survived is the middle register: quiet enough to trust, specific enough to remember. The site was restructured twice after the direction shipped: the homepage era-timeline and its standalone Career page were removed (the career narrative now lives as prose on the renamed About page), the standalone Apps page folded into a homepage 'Shipped apps' section, the footer was stripped to copyright-only with every link moved to the header nav, and the header brand changed from a text wordmark to an image badge.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground with exactly one warm accent color, never a second competing hue
Glass-material cards (translucent tint + blur) instead of drop-shadow elevation
SF Pro system stack throughout — no imported display face
Two-tier exponential entrance motion on load (calm for supporting content, faster+scaled for each page's h1); no bounce/overshoot, no ambient or decorative animation at rest
Hover affordance reserved strictly for elements that are actually clickable
Real evidence over illustration: every image on the site is a real screenshot or a real captured session

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Antique Gold is the only chromatic color in the system. Every other value is a neutral. A new element earns Antique Gold or it stays neutral.

rules.name: The Rarity Rule
rules.body: The accent covers a small minority of any given viewport at all times.

rules.name: The Single-Face Rule
rules.body: No second font family is introduced for any role. Distinction comes from weight and size only.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: No small uppercase label ever sits above a heading to introduce it, for any brief. Removed sitewide during finish review — the heading carries its own weight. A status badge that sits after a heading and adds new information stays allowed.

rules.name: The Two-Breakpoint Rule
rules.body: Every page-level grid collapses at exactly 900px and 560px. A third breakpoint value is drift.

rules.name: The Glass-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A new card gets a glass treatment by default. A drop-shadow is only added when it serves a specific, named purpose.

rules.name: The Honest Hover Rule
rules.body: A hover state is only ever added to an element that is actually a link or button. A purely informational card never gets the interactive treatment.

dos: Do keep Antique Gold to a strict minority of any viewport — one accent, spent rarely
Do use the glass-card treatment as the default for any new card; reach for a shadow only for a named purpose
Do add the .interactive modifier only to elements that are real links or buttons
Do collapse every new responsive grid at exactly 900px and 560px
Do use real screenshots or real captured sessions for any evidentiary image, with the standard 14px radius + Hairline border
Do keep every claim on the page backed by a real, checkable link or fact
donts: Don't introduce a second accent color, even for a one-off moment like an error or warning state
Don't add a drop-shadow as a default elevation device
Don't give a static, non-clickable card a hover state
Don't add an eyebrow or kicker above a heading, ever, for any brief
Don't put a link list back in the footer — the nav is the system's one and only link surface
